# Purpose

Award credit for a defensible engine-to-wing load path, a tapered fixed-root cantilever idealization, correct moment and torque resultants, consistent SI units, correct hollow-section properties, Hibbeler Section 5.7 thin-walled closed-section torsion, and an engineering conclusion explicitly limited to the static engine-weight contribution.

# Source and Input Distinctions

The engine dry mass is based on the GEnx-1B value listed in European Union Aviation Safety Agency Type Certificate Data Sheet IM.E.102, Issue 12, dated 25 February 2026. The calculation uses <em>g</em> = 9.81 m/s<sup>2</sup> as a fixed constant.

The wing-box dimensions, root-to-engine station, chordwise eccentricity, and equivalent wall thickness are instructor-assigned physically representative teaching values. They are not claimed as proprietary Boeing geometry and are not measured from the supplied photograph.

The closed-section torsion calculation follows Hibbeler, <em>Mechanics of Materials</em> (Pearson, 2022), Section 5.7: <em>q</em> = <em>T</em>/(2<em>A</em><sub>m</sub>) and &tau;<sub>avg</sub> = <em>T</em>/(2<em>tA</em><sub>m</sub>).

# Scope of the Base Problem

Use a fixed-root tapered cantilever, a concentrated engine mass, linear geometric taper, and a single-cell thin-walled rectangular closed section with uniform equivalent thickness. Exclude aerodynamic lift, fuel, wing self-weight, thrust, maneuver/gust and dynamic loads, fatigue, buckling, local pylon/attachment stresses, stress concentrations, detailed multicell geometry, composite anisotropy, failure criteria, and certification-level analysis.

# Faculty Template Verification Note

The faculty template's baseline list contains one typographical error: <em>M</em><sub>root</sub> is written once as 6.030 kN&middot;m. The governing equation and all downstream stresses require the dimensionally correct value, 603.030 kN&middot;m, which is used here.
